newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Paranapanema seeks partners abroad.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Paranapanema seeks partners abroad.

text.p: Brazilian metals group Paranapanema is holding talks with multinationals in the mining business in Argentina and Chile seeking partnerships to increase its copper output, a company official said.
"We have been talking with some international groups eyeing some partneships, maybe joint-ventures," said Dennis Braz Goncalves, president of Paranapanema group.
Goncalves said the partnerships would be in line with the group's strategy to strenghten their core business.
"Our business is tin, zinc and copper," said Goncalves.

Copper, which is produced by Paranapanema's unit Caraiba Metais, accounts for 60 percent of the group's total revenues, followed by semi-finished copper goods, with 20 percent; zinc, with 10 percent and tin with 10 percent.
Last week Paranapanema acquired Peru's polymetallic firm Empresa Minera Yauliyacu, which will provide its zinc unit Companhia Paraibuna de Metais with 40 percent of its zinc concentrate needs.
Paranapanema's zinc output is expected to rise to 75,000 tonnes in 1997, up from an estimated 65,000 tonnes this year, Goncalves said.
Paranapanema has also prequalified to bid for Bolivia's state-onwed Vinto tin smelter, scheduled to be auctioned off in January 1997.
With this acquisition, Paranapanema would double its stake in the international tin market, Goncalves said.
Currently, the Brazilian firm accounts for 10 percent of the world's tin output and 60 percent of the national production.

Goncalves also said Paranapanema group is investing 120 million reais in projects including the modernization and expansion of its units. He said 40 million reais were invested this year, while a total of 60 million reais will be invested in 1997 and the remainder will be allocated in 1998.
